pages.title: Treatments
pages.content:
Treatments

Six treatments,
one at a time.

What is offered this season

(01)WarmCool

A short list of six treatments, each held in its own quiet room. Please tell us about pregnancy, recent injuries or medication when booking.

Price list

Six treatments,
listed plainly.

In pounds sterling

We offer six treatments, each dedicated to unhurried care. The Quiet Hour Massage lasts 60 minutes for £85. The Long Stillness Massage offers 90 minutes of restorative touch for £120. Our Warm Stone Back Ritual runs 75 minutes for £98. The Face & Scalp Rest provides 50 minutes of focused stillness for £72. The Foot & Hand Calm runs 45 minutes for £58. Finally, Bath & Rest combines a 40-minute private soak with our Quiet Hour Massage across 120 minutes for £150. All appointments include tea in the lounge.

Treatment

(01)

Quiet Hour Massage

60 min · £85

The Quiet Hour Massage is our foundational full-body treatment, lasting 60 minutes for £85. We use warm, cold-pressed sweet almond and unfragranced camellia oils to release tension along the back, shoulders, neck, and limbs. It suits those seeking a reliable, steady pause from daily strain and mental fatigue. The rhythm remains unhurried throughout, allowing breathing to slow naturally. Please inform us of any muscular sensitivities, pregnancy, or recent injuries prior to beginning so we may adjust our pressure and support.

Treatment

(02)

Long Stillness Massage

90 min · £120

Extending across 90 minutes for £120, the Long Stillness Massage is designed for profound physical rest. This extended full-body massage uses light golden jojoba oil warmed to body temperature, giving ample time to work thoroughly through deep-seated tension in the hips, back, and shoulders without rushing. It suits anyone carrying persistent exhaustion or completing demanding work. Guests often drift into light sleep as the room remains warm and peaceful. A gentle herbal wash marks the conclusion before you rise.

Treatment

(03)

Warm Stone Back Ritual

75 min · £98

Lasting 75 minutes for £98, the Warm Stone Back Ritual focuses on easing chronic tightness across the back, neck, and shoulders. Smooth river stones are heated in water and applied along the spine over natural linen, accompanied by a blend of cedarwood and neutral carrier oils. The penetrating heat softens tight muscles before hands-on massage begins. It suits anyone spending long hours seated at desks or carrying heavy physical strain during colder months. The combination leaves the body deeply grounded.

(04)

Tea is served in the lounge after every treatment.

Treatment

(04)

Face & Scalp Rest

50 min · £72

The Face & Scalp Rest offers 50 minutes of concentrated relief for £72. Working with delicate squalane and jojoba oils, the therapist uses slow, measured fingertip movements across the brow, temples, jaw, neck, and scalp. It suits guests experiencing mental strain, tension headaches, jaw clenching, or fatigue from prolonged screen work. Pressure remains light to medium, encouraging immediate mental quiet. You remain comfortably supported beneath soft blankets while facial muscles soften and tension across the crown gently disperses.

Treatment

(05)

Foot & Hand Calm

45 min · £58

Running for 45 minutes for £58, Foot & Hand Calm attends to the body’s most worked extremities. The treatment begins with feet resting in a warm ceramic water basin before rhythmic massage is applied to the calves, ankles, soles, hands, and forearms using rich unperfumed shea and apricot kernel oils. It suits people who stand on their feet all day or work continuously with their hands. This treatment restores circulation, relieves joint stiffness, and induces a remarkable sense of whole-body calm.

Treatment

(06)

Bath & Rest

120 min · £150

Bath & Rest spans 120 minutes for £150, uniting our private soaking bath with the full Quiet Hour Massage. You begin with 40 uninterrupted minutes in the deep stone soaking tub filled with warm mineral water, allowing muscles to relax in solitude. Afterwards, your therapist guides you to your treatment room for an hour of quiet full-body massage using sweet almond oil. Please see our Rooms page for details on the soaking room. This pairing offers our most complete retreat.

See the soaking room

One quiet hour, held for you.

3 Linden Quay, Bristol BS1 4RN · Tuesday to Sunday, 10:00 to 20:00 · +44 117 496 0418

pages.title: Rooms
pages.content:
Rooms

Four rooms,
one bath.

Linen, window light, quiet

(02)LightShade

Yuragi houses four treatment rooms, one private stone soaking room, and a shared tea lounge. Each room is reset with clean linen and aired for twelve minutes between guests.

Room

(01)

Room 01 Linen

Rear courtyard, linen hangings

Room 01 Linen is situated near the quiet rear courtyard, defined by natural unbleached linen hangings and pale ash timber fittings. The room contains a wide, heated treatment bed made with crisp cotton sheets, a wool blanket, and soft indirect lighting. Filtered morning light enters through high windows, creating a peaceful, muted atmosphere for massage. Like all our rooms, it is fully private, acoustically isolated, and held at an even, comfortable warmth throughout your appointment.

Room

(02)

Room 02 Cedar

Cedar panelling, stone counter

Room 02 Cedar is lined with simple western red cedar panelling that releases a faint, grounding wood scent into the quiet air. Designed particularly for longer rituals and stone work, the space includes a stone-topped preparation counter and dimmable sconce lighting. Soft linen curtains shield the window, maintaining gentle shade during the day. The treatment bed is dressed with freshly laundered linens, providing an undisturbed sanctuary where you can fully disconnect from the city outside.

Room

(03)

Room 03 Clay

Clay plaster, quiet stillness

Room 03 Clay features smooth, hand-troweled lime and clay plaster walls that diffuse sound and soften daylight. This room offers a cocoon of quiet comfort, furnished only with a treatment bed, a low ash stool, and hooks for your clothing. The muted earthy palette calms the visual senses, making it particularly suitable for restorative stillness and scalp treatments. The room is thoroughly aired and sanitized between appointments, ensuring a fresh, clean space for every guest.

Room

(04)

Room 04 Window

Ground floor, step-free

Room 04 Window is located on the ground floor with complete step-free access from the street entrance. Large frosted glass panes admit generous daylight while preserving total privacy from Linden Quay. Equipped with a versatile treatment table that adjusts easily for individual mobility needs, this room welcomes any guest requiring accessible appointments. Warm cotton blankets, quiet ventilation, and understated stone decor create an unhurried, comfortable space dedicated entirely to your treatment and peace of mind.

Room

(05)

The Soaking Room

Deep stone bath, tall window

Our private soaking room features a deep grey stone bath, carved from solid stone and filled with clear, warm water. Light steam rises toward the tall ceiling, illuminated by natural daylight from a high frosted window. The room includes a low wooden washing stool, a ceramic basin, and hooks holding a freshly laundered waffle-weave robe and felt slippers. Guests booking our Bath & Rest ritual spend forty quiet minutes here in total privacy before their massage begins.

(07)

Four rooms and one bath. The linen is changed for every guest.

Room

(06)

The Tea Lounge

Long bench, wide windows

The tea lounge welcomes guests upon arrival and offers a calm resting space after treatments. Furnished with a long low timber bench beneath wide windows facing the Bristol sky, the lounge invites you to pause without haste. Here you are served seasonal roasted green tea or light herbal infusions in ceramic bowls. Guests are encouraged to linger for twenty minutes or longer, sipping warm tea, reading, or simply watching the daylight change across Linden Quay.

One quiet hour, held for you.

3 Linden Quay, Bristol BS1 4RN · Tuesday to Sunday, 10:00 to 20:00 · +44 117 496 0418

pages.title: Booking
pages.content:
Booking

How a time
is held for you.

Four quiet steps

(03)The weekOne hour

Reserving an appointment at Yuragi is straightforward, deposit-free, and held entirely in trust. We welcome bookings online, by telephone, or via email.

Phone

+44 117 496 0418

Email

hello@yuragi.example

Hours

Tuesday to Sunday, 10:00 to 20:00 (last booking 18:30; closed Mondays)

Part

(01)

Choose a Treatment

Six treatments, one at a time

Review our concise list of six treatments and select the duration and focus that fits your current needs. Whether you reserve the 60-minute Quiet Hour Massage for £85, the 75-minute Warm Stone Back Ritual for £98, or the 120-minute Bath & Rest for £150, every session is delivered one guest at a time. If you are uncertain which therapy suits your physical state, our reception staff can describe each option in detail and assist your choice.

Part

(02)

Hold a Time

Online, phone or email

Appointments may be held through our simple online booking portal, by calling +44 117 496 0418, or by emailing hello@yuragi.example. We do not take advance deposits; your appointment is held on trust. When booking, please inform us of any relevant health considerations, injuries, or pregnancy. Our team will promptly confirm your date and time, providing clear arrival notes so you can look forward to an effortless visit from the moment you reserve.

Part

(03)

Arrival and Preparation

Fifteen minutes early

We ask that you arrive fifteen minutes before your scheduled start time. This buffer allows you to hang your coat, store your shoes and mobile phone in a lounge locker, and change into our comfortable robes and slippers. You will complete a brief paper health questionnaire while sipping a warm welcome tea. Arriving early ensures your treatment starts promptly without sacrificing a single minute of your hands-on massage time in the room.

Part

(04)

Post-Treatment Rest and Vouchers

Tea, as long as you like

When your treatment concludes, there is no need to rush back into the street. We invite you to spend twenty minutes or more in the tea lounge enjoying fresh herbal tea and water. For payment, we accept card transactions at reception before you leave. If you hold a gift voucher, simply present your voucher code or printed card. Yuragi gift vouchers remain valid for twelve months from purchase and cover any listed treatment.

(05)

Stay in the lounge as long as you like.

Policy

Cancellation Policy

Free until 24 hours before

We understand that schedules shift unexpectedly. Cancellations or rescheduling requests made at least 24 hours prior to your appointment are completely free of charge. If you cancel within 24 hours of your booking time or do not attend, a fee equal to 50% of the scheduled treatment price will be charged. This policy respects our therapists' dedicated preparation and allows us to offer opened room slots to waiting guests.

One quiet hour, held for you.

3 Linden Quay, Bristol BS1 4RN · Tuesday to Sunday, 10:00 to 20:00 · +44 117 496 0418

pages.title: First visit
pages.content:
First visit

Before you
arrive.

Fifteen minutes early

(01)ArriveSettle

Coming to Yuragi for the first time is designed to feel unhurried and clear from the moment you step off Linden Quay. Here is what to expect during your initial appointment.

Arrival

(01)

Arriving Fifteen Minutes Early

Tea first

Please plan to arrive at 3 Linden Quay fifteen minutes before your treatment time. When you step through our timber door and linen curtain, reception host Mei Lin Park will welcome you and guide you into the tea lounge. Arriving early ensures you never feel rushed. You will be served a cup of warm roasted tea, allowing your breath to settle and your transition from the Bristol streets to begin smoothly before your session starts.

Arrival

(02)

Paper Health Questionnaire

On paper, in your words

Before your therapist takes you to your room, you will complete a brief paper health questionnaire. We ask about muscular aches, medical conditions, medications, recent surgeries, and pregnancy, as well as pressure preferences. Yuragi makes no medical claims. The form simply records what you tell us, so the session can be adjusted to your notes. Your therapist reviews those notes with you privately in the treatment room before any touch begins, so pressure and support follow what you have written.

(03)

A quiet corridor, four doors and a linen curtain.

Arrival

(03)

Robes, Slippers, and Lockers

Quiet, switched off

We provide washed linen robes and soft felt slippers for your visit. Secure wooden lockers are located beside the lounge where you can leave your coat, outdoor shoes, bags, and mobile phone. We ask all guests to switch phones off or set them to silent to preserve the building’s quiet. During massage treatments, you disrobe in private to your comfort level beneath fresh cotton sheets and blankets; only the area being massaged is ever uncovered.

Arrival

(04)

Post-Treatment Tea Lounge

Twenty minutes or more

Following your treatment, your therapist leaves the room so you can dress unhurriedly. You are then guided back to our peaceful tea lounge, hosted by Sunniva Berg. We encourage you to rest here for approximately twenty minutes or as long as your schedule permits. Savoring hot tea by the window allows the benefits of the oils and quietness to settle into your muscles, ensuring you return to the city relaxed and refreshed.

One quiet hour, held for you.

3 Linden Quay, Bristol BS1 4RN · Tuesday to Sunday, 10:00 to 20:00 · +44 117 496 0418

pages.content:
People

Seven people,
four rooms.

Who is in the rooms

(02)HandsQuiet

Seven dedicated individuals care for Yuragi's four treatment rooms, soaking bath, and tea lounge. Each team member brings quiet attention, warmth, and steady hands to every appointment.

Founder

Ines Kovač,
since 2017.

Founder and therapist

Ines Kovač

Founder & Therapist · Since 2017

Ines founded Yuragi in 2017 after converting a former dockside linen warehouse on Linden Quay. With over fifteen years of therapeutic bodywork practice, she oversees our treatment design and therapist training. Ines believes that true hospitality lies in quiet consistency, natural materials, and unhurried pacing. When in the treatment room, she offers the Quiet Hour Massage and Long Stillness sessions, focusing on restoring ease to tired bodies with calm, measured, rhythmic strokes.

The rooms

Six more
pairs of hands.

Therapists and hosts

Theo Marchetti

Lead Therapist · Since 2017

Theo joined Yuragi at its opening in 2017 and serves as our lead therapist. He specialises in deep muscular release and restorative full-body treatments. His quiet, grounded approach helps guests release chronic physical tension held across the neck, upper shoulders, and lower back. Theo also works closely with Ines to ensure our linen standards, room warmth, and twelve-minute reset intervals are meticulously maintained across every single shift of the working week.

Amara Osei

Therapist, Face & Scalp · Since 2018

Amara has been with Yuragi since 2018, bringing precise technique and gentle attentiveness to our treatment rooms. She developed our Face & Scalp Rest ritual, focusing on easing tension in the temples, cranial fascia, and jawline using natural plant squalane. Guests frequently comment on her reassuring touch and ability to induce quiet calm. Amara also provides our Quiet Hour and Long Stillness massages with dedicated care and thoughtful presence.

Lena Hoffmann

Therapist · Since 2019

Lena joined our therapeutic team in 2019, bringing extensive experience in holistic bodywork and restorative touch. She delivers the Quiet Hour Massage, Long Stillness Massage, and Foot & Hand Calm with exceptional rhythm and steady pressure. Lena takes great care to understand each guest’s physical state through their intake questionnaire, ensuring every session provides an undisturbed space where muscles unwind naturally and breathing slows to a gentle, comfortable rhythm.

Rafael Ortega

Therapist, Warm Stones · Since 2020

Rafael joined Yuragi in 2020, specialising in thermo-therapy and our Warm Stone Back Ritual. He oversees the preparation, water temperature, and careful placement of smooth basalt river stones, pairing heat with grounding cedarwood oil. Rafael’s sessions offer profound relief for guests carrying stubborn stiffness from sedentary desk work or athletic exertion. His calm demeanor and attentive presence ensure every guest feels entirely safe, supported, and deeply rested throughout their time.

Mei Lin Park

Bookings & Reception · Since 2019

Mei Lin has managed Yuragi's reception desk and guest communications since 2019. She is usually the first voice you hear on the telephone and the warm presence who greets you at the Linden Quay entrance. Mei Lin handles all scheduling, gift voucher inquiries, and special accommodation requests with calm efficiency. Her thoughtful organization ensures that the reception desk remains a serene, welcoming point of arrival without clutter or rush.

Sunniva Berg

Rooms & Tea Lounge Host · Since 2021

Sunniva joined Yuragi in 2021 to oversee our tea lounge and ensure our treatment rooms are impeccably cared for. She prepares our seasonal green and herbal teas, tends the lounge seating, and manages the linen turnaround between guests. Sunniva looks after the turnaround so that fresh towels, clean robes, and clean stone surfaces are ready for the next visitor, and the step from the treatment room back toward the street stays quiet and unhurried.

One quiet hour, held for you.

pages.title: About
pages.content:
About

A short list,
kept short.

Since 2017 on Linden Quay

(03)CityStillness

Yuragi was established in 2017 to offer a quiet, unhurried sanctuary along the Bristol floating harbour. We believe true hospitality is found in doing a few essential things with deep attention.

Story

(01)

Founded in 2017 on Linden Quay

A former linen warehouse

In 2017, founder Ines Kovač discovered a former dockside linen warehouse at 3 Linden Quay in Bristol. The building’s thick brick walls, timber floorboards, and high ceilings offered natural quiet just moments away from the city centre. With care, the interior was converted into four private treatment rooms, a stone soaking bath, and a timber tea lounge. We chose the name Yuragi to reflect gentle swaying, natural fluctuation, and the return of the body to equilibrium.

Story

(02)

Why We Keep a Short List

Six, done well

Many spas present dozens of complex treatments, exotic add-ons, and technical machinery. At Yuragi, we intentionally limit our menu to just six focused therapies. By maintaining a short list, our therapists master every stroke, transition, and oil application. We do not use noisy machines or promote miracle cures. Instead, we concentrate entirely on skilled touch, unhurried timing, high-quality plant oils, and quiet rooms where guests can reliably let go of tension.

(03)

A long bench, a wide window and two cups of tea.

Story

(03)

Why Four Rooms

Four rooms and one bath

We deliberately built only four treatment rooms and one private soaking room within our spacious building. Keeping our capacity small ensures the spa never feels crowded or hurried. You will rarely encounter more than two or three other guests in the lounge. This intimate scale allows our seven staff members to care for every visitor personally, providing quiet check-ins, freshly brewed tea, and private spaces where stillness is never compromised by foot traffic.

Story

(04)

The Twelve-Minute Reset

Twelve minutes between guests

Between every appointment, we reserve a strict twelve-minute reset interval during which no treatments take place. During these twelve minutes, the room is aired thoroughly with fresh quay air, all surfaces are sanitized, and every sheet, towel, and blanket is replaced with clean linen. The interval is there so therapists are not asked to hurry from one guest to the next. They enter the next session with the room aired, and you enter a room that has been made quiet and ready again.

One quiet hour, held for you.

pages.title: Questions
pages.content:
Questions

Asked often,
answered plainly.

Ten short answers

(03)AskEase

Practical answers to common questions about appointments, accessibility, and our quiet rooms. If you have an inquiry not answered below, please call or email our reception.

What should I wear during my treatment?

We provide freshly laundered waffle linen robes and felt slippers upon your arrival in the lounge. During treatments, you disrobe in total privacy to your individual comfort level. Most guests choose to remove outer clothing while keeping their underwear on. Throughout the entire massage, you remain covered under warm cotton sheets and blankets; your therapist only uncovers the specific limb, shoulder, or section of the back currently receiving hands-on touch.

What happens if I arrive late?

If you arrive late for your scheduled booking, we will do our best to provide as much of your treatment as possible within the remaining allotted time. However, to respect the twelve-minute reset interval and ensure our next booked guest begins promptly, your session cannot be extended beyond its scheduled finish time. Full treatment fees apply. We strongly recommend arriving fifteen minutes early to enjoy tea and avoid feeling rushed.

Can two people book a treatment together in the same room?

We do not offer couples rooms or simultaneous treatments in the same space. Yuragi is designed around deep individual rest, and each of our four treatment rooms is built for exactly one guest at a time. If you wish to visit alongside a companion, we are happy to schedule concurrent appointments in separate private rooms, allowing you to meet before and after your sessions to share tea in the lounge.

Can I receive a treatment while pregnant?

Please notify us of your pregnancy when making your reservation. We offer adapted massage treatments after the first trimester (past twelve weeks) that support maternal comfort and physical ease. Our therapists use gentle positioning, supportive pillows, and safe, unperfumed neutral oils such as sweet almond or jojoba. We do not perform deep abdominal work or intensive warm stone treatments during pregnancy. If you have medical concerns, please consult your doctor first.

What is the minimum age for treatments?

All guests visiting Yuragi must be aged 18 or older. Our quiet day spa is conceived exclusively as an adult sanctuary dedicated to silent contemplation, restorative bodywork, and stillness. We do not accommodate infants, children, or teenagers under 18 years of age in our treatment rooms, soaking bath, or tea lounge, ensuring an undisturbed atmosphere for everyone seeking respite from everyday responsibilities.

What if I have allergies or sensitivities to massage oils?

Please inform us of any skin sensitivities, contact allergies, or nut allergies on your paper health questionnaire and during booking. While our standard treatments use pure sweet almond, squalane, or jojoba oils, we keep cold-pressed camellia oil and pure apricot kernel oil available as nut-free and hypoallergenic alternatives. We use no synthetic fragrances, artificial preservatives, or harsh chemical additives in any of our rooms or bathing rituals.

Is tipping expected at Yuragi?

Tipping is not expected or required. Our service pricing is fully inclusive and transparent, reflecting fair, dignified compensation for our skilled therapists and front-of-house team. The price listed on our treatment menu is the exact total you pay at reception upon departure. The greatest compliment you can offer our team is your return visit or recommending our quiet rooms to friends and colleagues in Bristol.

Is the spa wheelchair accessible?

Yes. Yuragi features a step-free entrance directly from the street level on Linden Quay. Room 04 Window is located on the ground floor with wide door frames, level thresholds, and an adjustable treatment table designed to accommodate visitors with reduced mobility or wheelchair users comfortably. Our reception and ground-floor restroom facilities are also fully accessible. Please notify us when booking so we reserve Room 04 for your arrival.

Where do I leave my mobile phone and personal belongings?

Secure private wooden lockers are located directly adjacent to our tea lounge. Upon arrival, you receive a key to store your coat, shoes, bags, and personal belongings safely. We kindly ask all visitors to turn their mobile phones off or switch them to silent mode before storing them. Keeping phones inside lockers protects the quiet privacy of our rooms and allows you to disconnect fully during your stay.

What is your cancellation and rescheduling policy?

You may cancel or reschedule your reservation free of charge up to 24 hours prior to your scheduled start time by calling +44 117 496 0418 or emailing hello@yuragi.example. If you cancel within 24 hours of your appointment or fail to attend, a cancellation fee equal to 50% of the booked treatment price is charged. This policy allows us to maintain fair compensation for therapists whose time is reserved.

One quiet hour, held for you.

posts.title: Why We Still Fold Every Towel by Hand
posts.excerpt: Folding linen by hand is not a design flourish; it is the quiet ritual that prepares our rooms and minds for the next guest.
posts.content:
Every morning at nine o'clock, an hour before the front door opens on Linden Quay, the treatment rooms at Yuragi are completely silent. Sunlight filters through the linen curtains onto pale ash floorboards. On the timber counter of the back room sits a fresh stack of washed white cotton towels, still faintly warm from drying. We could easily stack them quickly or use commercial pre-folded packs, but we choose instead to fold each one slowly by hand. Two hands square the fabric, aligning the woven borders until the edges meet with clean precision.

To an outsider, spending twenty minutes every morning smoothing towels might appear inefficient. In modern commercial hospitality, automated speed and outsourced linen services are standard practice. Yet at Yuragi, we have kept this practice unchanged since opening our doors in 2017. Founder Ines Kovač established the ritual during our very first month in the former dockside warehouse. Folding linen is not an aesthetic performance for visitors; it is a physical discipline that prepares our therapists for the quiet attentiveness their work requires.

Therapeutic bodywork cannot be rushed. If a therapist enters a treatment room with a distracted mind or racing heartbeat, the guest feels that tension immediately through the touch of their hands. The act of smoothing cotton against wood requires your complete tactile attention. You feel the weight of the weave, press out small creases, and align the hem. For twelve minutes between guests, as rooms are aired and reset, folding clean linen acts as a mental reset. It empties the mind of the previous hour and restores a quiet, receptive focus for the guest who is about to arrive.

The towels themselves are chosen for their simple, durable honesty. We use heavy unbleached cotton that absorbs moisture cleanly and feels reassuringly substantial when placed across shoulders or limbs. During a treatment, these towels create boundaries of warmth and privacy. When a guest lies face down on the bed, feeling the weight of folded cotton across their lower back provides an immediate sensation of security. It signals to the nervous system that the surrounding space is safe, private, and held in stillness.

Our seven therapists and lounge hosts share this duty throughout the working week. Whether it is Sunniva preparing fresh linens for the soaking room, Theo setting up Room 01 before a Long Stillness appointment, or Ines checking the treatment tables between guests, the rhythm remains identical. We do not use scented laundry detergents or artificial fabric softeners; the fabric carries only the clean, neutral scent of fresh air and steam. Touching the linen directly keeps our standards grounded in the physical reality of human comfort rather than abstract checklist procedures.

When you step into Room 01 or Room 02, you see only the quiet result: a perfectly aligned edge resting at the foot of the bed, a folded robe on a timber peg, and a clean ceramic basin of warm water. You do not see the deliberate hands that prepared them fifteen minutes earlier. But that quiet preparation is what allows the room to hold you. In a city where life moves rapidly, having a space where nothing is hurried and every detail has been touched with care makes all the difference. That is why we continue to fold every towel by hand, one quiet fold at a time.
